title: Baked Pork Spring Rolls
subtitle: Crispy Chinese-style rolls without deep frying
excerpt: Pork mince, shredded cabbage, carrot, and ginger rolled in gyoza wrappers and baked until crisp. Baking rather than deep frying requires careful oiling but produces a lighter result that is easy to make for a crowd.
sourceNotes: Spring rolls are eaten across China and throughout Southeast Asia in many forms, from the thin crispy Cantonese style to the fresh, uncooked Vietnamese version. This recipe uses gyoza wrappers as a practical home substitute for spring roll wrappers, which can be harder to find.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked on a lined tray, then transfer to a bag. Bake from frozen at 200C, adding 5 to 8 minutes to the cooking time.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and freeze half unbaked for another time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 4 hours ahead and keep covered in the fridge. Brush with oil just before baking.

content.text: The filling must be completely cool before rolling or the wrappers will steam and become soggy. Cook the filling, spread it out on a tray, and leave for 10 minutes before assembling. Brush the rolls very generously with oil on all sides before baking; this is what creates the golden, crispy exterior.
Heat a dry frying pan over a high heat. Add the pork mince and break it up, cooking for 5 minutes until browned. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cabbage, carrot, and spring onion. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until the vegetables have wilted. Add the soy sauce and sesame oil, toss to combine, then spread onto a tray to cool completely.
Preheat the oven to 200C. Line a baking tray with baking paper.

Lay a gyoza wrapper on a clean surface. Place 1.5 to 2 tbsp of filling along the bottom third. Fold the bottom edge up over the filling, fold in the sides, and roll tightly. Seal the edge with a dab of water. Repeat for all 12 rolls.
Place the rolls seam-side down on the lined tray. Brush all over generously with sunflower oil.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and crispy. Serve with rice vinegar and soy sauce for dipping.

items.symptom: Rolls are not crispy, just chewy.
items.cause: Not enough oil on the outside before baking.
items.fix: Brush every surface generously with oil before going into the oven.

items.cause: Too much filling was used, or the seal was not tight enough.
items.fix: Use less filling and press the seam down firmly with a damp finger.

items.symptom: Filling is wet and soggy inside.
items.cause: The filling had not cooled before rolling, creating steam.
items.fix: Spread filling on a tray and cool fully before assembling.
